Definition: properly, redundant; hence, over and above, as adjective, noun, adverb or conjunction
BiblicalUsage: yôwthêr means properly, redundant. In Esther 6:6 we read, "So Haman came in." It appears again in Ecclesiastes 2:15: "Then said I in my heart, As it happeneth to the fool, so it happeneth even to me; and why was I then more wise?"
TheologicalSignificance: yowther is properly, redundant, and my position is that the plain words matter as much as the great ones, because God gave them all.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
